query: The Cold Snap A hard frost is coming tonight, the first of the season. Your seedling is too young for it. Somebody would have to sit with it till dawn, feeding it warmth. Sit up with it all night You sit wrapped round the lantern till dawn, feeding it what warmth you have. By morning you're stiff and coughing, and the seedling has grown a thorn, which it seems proud of. Cover it and hope You cover it with sacking and go to bed. It survives, sulking, and loses a leaf. It is noticeably cooler towards you.

Cold Things Think Twice
The cold comes into the castle tonight like something looking for someone. Frost runs along the corridor windows ahead of you, then stops at your feet and goes round, as if it had remembered its manners. Your collar, where Ilse's ward is sewn, is warm.
